FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 145
Committee: Economic Development and Tourism Sponsor: Representative Adline Clarke
Analyst: Mathieu Fuller Date: 03/04/2025
House Bill 145 as introduced could: (1) increase the obligations of the city of Mobile by an
undetermined amount dependent upon the costs to establish a local program to enforce the
provisions of the Alabama Scrap Tire Environmental Quality Act which could be offset by any
funds received from the Alabama Department of Environmental Management (ADEM) from
delegation agreements; and (2) decrease the administrative obligations of ADEM for delegating
enforcement of that act in the city of Mobile.
This bill could also increase receipts to the State General Fund and municipal general funds
from fines; increase receipts to the State General Fund, county general funds, municipal general
funds, and other funds to which court costs are deposited; and could increase the obligations of
the State General Fund, district attorneys, and local jails by an undetermined amount dependent
upon the number of persons charged with and convicted of the offenses provided by this bill and
the penalties imposed.
